criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: The register is bold and consistent. Near-black fields, light type on dark, and one cold flood from the upper right. machine_qa bands sit dark on every frame, and the TXBENCH reliefs on 5, 6 and 7 report 5 to 6 materials and height ranges of 31.6 to 114 with real casts. Slide 7's county relief is the strongest image in the deck at feed size: a raked clay map, the white Dallas to Houston inlay casting a shadow, and rust studs to Laredo. Slide 1 stops the thumb: a white tractor on the scale deck, yellow kerb rails converging, a green signal and the scale house. Slide 9 reads as built against expected (20 white-stall tractors, counted 10+10 in the full render, under primer rows running into the dark). But more than one frame leans on a default, which is below the 7 descriptor. Slide 8's kit tractor reads toy-like under a blue-violet cast. Its beacon is a dull yellow dome with little spill and no ground, so 'stopped' is never shown. Slide 3 leaves the right half of the middle band dead dark, with the boom and yellow bollard floating and no checkpoint structure. Slide 6's loss bar is a mid-grey textured slab with no bright edge, and the $9 million scribe is nearly invisible at 432 px. At feed size slide 5's rule reads as a row of grey wall panels rather than a graduated rule.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: As a filmstrip it is clearly one deck. One night world, one key with casts to the lower left, one grade, and the steel, concrete and primer vocabulary. The rust accent keeps one meaning on 3, 5, 6, 7 and 9: expected and not yet done. The storyboard names motif evolution (scale deck to rule to datum to stall paint) and a camera move (yard on 4, the same yard from the mast on 9), and both are visible in the contact sheet. Value holds dark with no strobe. Slide 7's map and slide 6's slab sit slightly outside the spatial frames around them, and slide 8's purple cast is the one off-grade frame.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral traces to a claim, and every claim is primary: the SEC-filed letter, plus Aurora's own release for c21. On 4 that is 20+, 500,000 and 100% (c1, c2). On 5, six weeks and 20 a week (c12, c11). On 6, $3M, $257M and $9M (c13, c14, c12). On 7, 500, 2027 and 2028 (c3, c4, c19). On 8, five-year (c20). On 9, 200, 1,000 and October 28th (c15, c16). Round 1's slide 7 hard fail is gone: the headline 'Aurora's own route, and a customer's plan' counts nothing, and Dallas to Laredo stays future tense as Charger's plan. Company figures are attributed ('by Aurora's own count' on 4, 'the letter says' throughout). Two phrasings run looser than their source. Slide 1's headline states Aurora's self-reported capability as fact, with attribution only in the dek. Slide 3's 'straight through the gate' is stronger than c6's 'automated navigation through security checkpoints', though the image's lowered boom tempers it. Slide 9's 'Each primer stall is one expected truck' can't be checked by eye, since far fewer than 1,000 stalls are visible before the field fades. render_report 'encodings' is empty on every frame, so nothing machine-confirms the drawn counts beyond the storyboard's intent.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A reader learns what happened: Aurora's letter claims weigh station traversal, site-to-site runs in November, a ramp about six weeks late and a $257M quarterly loss. The decider is a company, and the docket's public_access is honestly contact_only with no process and no deadline. The Texas tie doesn't arrive until frame 7, so for six swipes this reads as an investor letter rather than a Texas story. No frame says whether the scale capability touches a Texas station. The web edition says the letter names none, but the deck never tells the reader that. The Texan stake is implied rather than stated. Frame 6's revenue and loss matter to a shareholder more than to a Texan. The one action offered is 'The filing is on the SEC's EDGAR site' on frame 9, plus the caption's question.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover earns the swipe, and frame 2 pays at once with the three calls placed on one station. The declared value cut at frame 5 is a real turn, and the close lands on built against expected. Frame 8 (the beacon) is a detour back to capability after the map. It could move to sit with 1 to 3, or be cut, without loss. Frame 7, the only place frame, comes late.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: There is good Texan register: 'The truck can now tell if the scale is open', 'Next, straight through the gate', and the caption's 'Has a Texas scale house weighed a driverless Aurora truck yet?'. The caption is clean, with no year on October 28th, no colons and no banned words. Several dek lines are production notes a reader never asked for: slide 7's 'Routes drawn straight between places. New Braunfels is marked at Comal County's center.', slide 6's fragment 'Third quarter revenue and operating loss at one scale.', and slide 9's 'Each primer stall is one expected truck.' A Texan does not know that 'primer' is this deck's colour code. That is three flat, machine-sounding lines, against the descriptor's one.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The weigh station concept and the mixed spatial and relief build are fresh against the last four decks. The familiar moves stack up, though. A white vehicle carried through a night world appeared in no. 66, no. 52 and no. 41. No. 41, on October 3rd, was a Kodiak driverless tractor and 53 ft van on Dallas to Houston, 31 days ago, one day outside the dedupe window.

named_defects: Slide 8: kit tractor reads toy-like under a blue-violet cast, the beacon has little visible glow, and there is no ground or shoulder, so 'when it stops' is not shown.
Slide 6: loss bar is a flat mid-grey slab with no bright edge, and the $9 million primer scribe is nearly invisible at 432 px.
Slide 3: dead dark right half of the middle band, with no checkpoint structure beside the boom.
Slide 5: at feed size the steel rule reads as a row of grey wall panels.
Slide 9 dek: 'Each primer stall is one expected truck' uses an internal colour term and asserts a count a reader can't see.
Slide 7 and slide 6 deks: method notes read as machine production notes.
No frame says the letter names no Texas weigh station or customer site, and the Texas place arrives only at frame 7.
storyboard.md slide 7 yaml dek is stale (the judge's reading).
Variety: a driverless truck on Dallas to Houston repeats the subject class of no. 41, 31 days back.
one_sentence_fix: Move the Texas corridor relief up from frame 7 to frame 3 and give it a plain line saying the letter names no Texas weigh station or customer site, then cut the method-note deks on 6, 7 and 9.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Kit tractor under a blue-violet cast reads as a toy. The beacon is a dull yellow dome with little spill, and with no ground or empty lane the frame doesn't show a stopped truck.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Make the cab_beacon strongly emissive with an amber point light that rakes the roof, hood and a strip of asphalt. Lower the camera so the dark shoulder and an empty lane appear in the bottom third. Neutralise the violet fill.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The loss bar is a mid-grey textured slab with no bright edge, and the $9 million mark on the datum vanishes at feed size.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Lower the bar's albedo toward blued black and give its top bevel a raking key highlight. Raise the $9 million scribe into a primer stud with height and a cast on the datum.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The right half of the middle band is empty dark. The boom and yellow bollard float with no checkpoint structure.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: In slide-03's own camera, yaw right and pull back so the boom's pivot cabinet and its pool of light fill the right third.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: At feed size the rule reads as a row of flat grey wall panels.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Narrow the rule, cut the six grooves deeper with lit upper edges, and drop the concrete above the rule darker.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Twenty tractors sit as a small icon array across the middle band.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Keep the frontal view that shows all 20, narrow the fov and drop the camera slightly so the near rank fills the lower third.
